title: Telangana Congress mobilises cadres for Delhi protest against Election Commission

tea.why: Protesting against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and the Chief Election Commissioner.
tea.want: To register opposition against electoral roll revisions and constitutional institutions.
tea.changed: Oct 30: Telangana BJP president dismissed claims that workers were being stopped from travelling to Delhi.

summary: The Telangana Congress is organising preparations to mobilise about 10,000 party cadres for a rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1. The demonstration targets Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, and the Election Commission of India. Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, and other senior leaders held district coordination meetings. Organisers arranged around 50 buses after the Railway Department declined to provide special trains. Meanwhile, the Telangana Bharatiya Janata Party dismissed the mobilisation as a political drama and accused the Congress of spreading false narratives against constitutional institutions.
demands: Oppose the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
response: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao dismissed the protest as political drama, denied claims that workers were being blocked from travelling, and accused the Congress of defaming constitutional institutions.

updates.text: Telangana Congress announced plans to mobilise 10,000 cadres for a November 1 rally in New Delhi.
Telangana BJP dismissed claims that Congress workers were being stopped from travelling to Delhi.
